claim: jev-ultrafast is a complete Python browser-agent loop, not an MCP server.
Its primary speed technique is reducing each browser step to a bounded operation and target decision, not making browser I/O intrinsically faster.
Operation and speculative operation-specific targets are evaluated in one TypeSafe request, after which code uses only the matching target head.
Free text generation remains necessary for TYPE_TEXT and is delegated to a separate small LLM.
The model cannot invent an executable selector or coordinate because execution resolves only code-owned observed node identities.
The current implementation records Jev confidence but does not gate execution on a confidence threshold.
DONE is not proof of task completion; production use requires an independent verifier.
The published speed result is narrow and insufficient to establish broad browser-agent reliability.
For YBA, the pattern is reusable but the repository is not a drop-in replacement for Playwright MCP.
